question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact grammar and scheme limits are safe for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: This would broaden a browser-origin authorization boundary for Gateway WebSocket and trusted-proxy HTTP paths, and current docs intentionally expose only full-origin entries plus the global `*`.

options.title: Approve constrained extension wildcard grammar
options.body: Define a small explicit grammar for extension-scheme wildcards, implement it in `checkBrowserOrigin`, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Fold into broader origin patterns
options.body: Wait for the loopback pattern work to settle and decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in the same public config contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained extension wildcard grammar
recommendation.body: Define a small explicit grammar for extension-scheme wildcards, implement it in `checkBrowserOrigin`, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.
